chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him (peace be upon him): 'If a pregnant woman, her husband having died, gives birth and then marries before completing the waiting period of four months and ten days,' he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the one who married her has consummated the marriage with her, they are separated, and she is not permissible for him ever; she completes the remainder of the waiting period of the first husband, and begins a new waiting period of three pure periods from the second husband. And if he has not consummated the marriage with her, they are separated, and she completes the remainder of her waiting period, and he is considered a suitor among suitors.'

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: He consummated the marriage with her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pregnant widow who remarries before completing her waiting period?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the complex jurisprudence of 'Iddah for a pregnant widow who remarries before the expiration of her waiting period, a scenario known as 'Iddah al-Hubla. It establishes that consummation with the second husband triggers a permanent prohibition (Tahrim) and requires her to complete the remainder of the first husband's Iddah before beginning a new three-cycle Iddah, whereas non-consummation leaves the second husband in the status of a suitor (Khatib). This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of the waiting period and the legal consequences of marital consummation during overlapping periods.
